logline: A bickering married couple in their late thirties wake up as 20-year-old university students in 1999, forcing them to confront what they really want from each other before fate brings them back together.

renewal.note: 12-episode limited run completed November 2018. Based on the webtoon 'Do It One More Time' by Hong Seung-pyo and Kim Hye-yeon. No continuation.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb rates it 8.1/10 with strong audience engagement. Critics praised Son Ho-jun and Jang Na-ra's chemistry and the show's emotional resonance for married viewers, while noting the time-travel mechanics are left unexplained.

pull_quotes.text: A beautiful example of how you can take a not-so-unique premise and still make an amazingly heart-touching drama.

seasons.review_body: Go Back Couple aired on KBS2 from October to November 2017 and found an audience that connected strongly with its premise: a couple whose marriage has curdled through years of accumulated resentment gets a second chance to meet each other again at university in 1999. Son Ho-jun and Jang Na-ra bring the right blend of comic frustration and buried tenderness to their roles. Critics noted that the show's emotional logic is more persuasive than its time-travel mechanics, which are left deliberately unexplained. At 12 episodes, it runs lean and avoids the pacing drag that afflicts longer Korean romances. The IMDb score of 8.1 reflects strong audience goodwill, particularly from viewers in established relationships who recognise the show's central marital exhaustion with uncomfortable accuracy.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A brisk setup that sketches the couple's domestic fatigue with dark comedy before the time-travel rupture lands. The contrast between the 2017 couple and their 1999 university selves is established swiftly and effectively.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The leads' first moment of recognising each other as twenty-year-olds - before their adult relationship began - sets up the show's emotional engine with genuine ingenuity.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale brings the time-travel thread and the emotional arc home with warmth rather than sentimentality, landing a resolution that earns its happy ending through actual character work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final choice each lead makes about the life they want reflects growth earned across all 12 episodes, not a third-act shortcut.
